title: Right mate for a single finite rational coefficient extension
statement: Fix a prime l, two finite extensions E and F of Q_l and a Q_l-algebra inclusion iota:E to F [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let f:X to Y be any morphism of schemes with l invertible in every residue field. On the recorded raw rational constructible categories [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], let R_E and R_F be supplied right adjoints to the rational derived pullbacks L_E and L_F of [def-sf-finite-rational-derived-operations], with specified adjunctions aE and aF. The literal Mathlib right mate under aE and aF of the inverse normalized rationalPullbackScalarComparison(l,E,F,iota,f) is an isomorphism. The scalar functors are exactly sfRationalScalarExtension with p=0 and the canonical prime nonzero proof. No algebraic closure, directed coefficient index, stage system, coherence family, uniqueness assertion, or existence of right adjoints is involved.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2; Proposition 6.8.14(2); Remark 6.8.15; finite-free coefficient argument in the parent coefficient-compatibility proof

proof.text: Apply rationalScalarExtension_isRightAdjoint separately at X and Y, obtaining the Mathlib chosen left adjoints U_X and U_Y with adjunctions bX and bY. Adjointness specifies these objects up to the unique compatible isomorphism used by the next step.

Apply rationalRestrictionPullback_unit to these adjunctions. It gives an isomorphism e:L_F U_X to U_Y L_E with the explicit unit equation for the inverse normalized scalar/pullback comparison alpha. Let delta be the inverse coefficient mate of alpha. The equation unit_mateEquiv_symm gives the same equation for delta. Injectivity of bX.homEquiv at every object identifies delta componentwise with e.hom, so delta is invertible.

Apply Mathlib iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv to bY, bX, aF, aE and delta. The coefficient mate of delta is alpha by the inverse law for mateEquiv. The identity therefore identifies the specified geometric right mate of alpha with conjugateEquiv (bY.comp aE) (aF.comp bX) delta. Conjugation preserves isomorphisms, so this literal mate is invertible for the supplied aE and aF. This is a complete Lean argument with no assertion of geometric right-adjoint existence.

proof_origin.place: T4 implements step 3 by unit_mateEquiv_symm, homEquiv injectivity, and iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv. The coefficient-adjunction and explicit unit-normalized restriction steps are isolated in the two named dependencies.

lean.statement:
theorem rationalPullbackScalar_rightMate_isIso
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E F : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    [Field F] [Algebra ℚ_[l] F] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] F]
    (ι : E →ₐ[ℚ_[l]] F) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x)]
    [∀ y : Y, Invertible (l : Y.residueField y)]
    (RE : sfRationalConstructibleCategory l E X ⥤ sfRationalConstructibleCategory l E Y)
    (RF : sfRationalConstructibleCategory l F X ⥤ sfRationalConstructibleCategory l F Y)
    (aE : rationalDerivedPullback l E f ⊣ RE)
    (aF : rationalDerivedPullback l F f ⊣ RF) :
    IsIso ((mateEquiv aE aF
      (TwoSquare.mk _ _ _ _ (rationalPullbackScalarComparison l E F ι f).inv)).natTrans)
